verdict.rationale: Obsidian offers programmatic access through an in-app TypeScript plugin API, including a Vault interface for working with files and folders. It also has a custom URI protocol for some actions, such as opening or creating notes, and a headless Sync client for agents and automated workflows. Because notes are plain Markdown files, they can also be edited directly on disk. However, nothing in the evidence shows an external API that covers everything the UI can do; the URI scheme is limited to 'various actions', and the plugin API runs inside the app. Missing for 10: a documented external/REST API, explicit UI-to-API feature parity, and independent hands-on corroboration of automation coverage.
